content.content:
**The fix status.** `fixStatusOf(f, onDisk)` (`details_fix.go`) says it in words, in a closed
vocabulary, never in a colour or a key name (Rules 130, 134). Every label is one of the five
constants, or `Built-in fix unavailable: ` followed by a non-empty reason
(`TestEveryFixLabelIsInTheClosedVocabulary`):

| Finding | Label | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| misconfiguration, the target is an image (catalog rule or not) | `Cannot fix here` | `reasonFileNotOnDisk`, in the footer on `ctrl+o` |
| misconfiguration, catalog rule, the rule declines this instance | `Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>` | the `Declines` reason |
| misconfiguration, catalog rule, directory, no refusal | `Built-in fix available` | Effect = `rule.Title`, Warning = `rule.Warning` |
| misconfiguration, no catalog rule, some guidance (`MissingFor`, Resolution or FixCommand) | `Manual` | Do = the missing text, then the Resolution |
| misconfiguration, no catalog rule, no guidance | `No guidance available` | |
| vulnerability with `FixedIn` | `Manual` | Effect = `Fixed in <version>` |
| vulnerability without | `No fix published` | |
| secret, license, CI | `Manual` with guidance, else `No guidance available` | |

A misconfiguration's status reads `misconfigFixAvailability` (extracted from `canFixMisconfig`),
so the status line, the `ctrl+o` shortcut and the footer refusal are one computation. The
invariants are tested: `Built-in fix available` holds exactly when `ctrl+o` is enabled in the
detail, and for `Built-in fix unavailable: R` and `Cannot fix here` the footer after `ctrl+o` is
exactly `R` and `reasonFileNotOnDisk` (`TestFixStatusAndTheShortcutAgree`,
`TestTheFooterAfterCtrlOSaysTheReasonOfTheFixLine`). A vulnerability with a `FixedIn` is
`Manual` because the vocabulary has no "fix available"; DEVDESK-750's `Fix available`,
`No fix available`, `No built-in fix`, `No built-in fix here` and `No built-in fix for this instance`
are gone.

**Command or sentence.** `scan.IsFixInstruction(f)` says whether `FixCommand` is the
`Update <pkg> to <version>` sentence written for an ecosystem with no known command
(`fixInstruction`, same bytes as before: the cache is unchanged). `fixAction` shows a
command as `Run: <cmd>` and a sentence as a step under `Do`. `runCommand(f)` is the one
computation behind the `Run` line and `Y`: the trimmed `FixCommand` when `fixAction` says `Run`
and it is plain words (`plainWords`), `("", false)` otherwise. It refuses a line break, any control
character (`unicode.IsControl`: an escape sequence, a tab, a carriage return, a NUL), any character
with no visible form or a blank other than a single space (`!unicode.IsPrint`: no-break space,
zero-width and right-to-left marks, line separator) and any shell metacharacter
(`shellMeta`: `; | & $ ` < > ( ) \ ' " { } * ? ! #`). The list is a second defense for a command that
did not come through `scan.FixCommand`, such as one read from a cache written by another build;
`TestRunCommandRefusesWhatAShellOrATerminalReadsAsMoreThanWords` holds its cases. A refused command
is not lost: `fixSteps` puts its text under `Do` like a sentence (control characters removed, see
below), `Y` is greyed with `reasonNoCommand`, and there is no `Run` line. The screen cuts the `Run`
line to the width of the column while `Y` copies all of it, which is why a tail could hide there
before this check.

**Scanner text on screen.** `normalizeText` and `oneLine` (`details_text.go`) go through
`withoutControlSpace`: an escape sequence (CSI, OSC) is removed whole with `ansi.Strip`, a tab
becomes four spaces, and every other control character (C0, C1, `\r`), line and paragraph separator
and format character (bidi and zero-width marks; the two joiners stay for emoji) is dropped. The line
feed stays for `normalizeText`. Nothing a scanner wrote can set the window title or reorder the text
(`TestNoScannerFieldReachesTheScreenWithAnEscapeSequence`).

**Actions from the detail (DEVDESK-751).** Six keys, the same for every finding, in this order:
`esc Back`, `W Open ref`, `enter Open file`, `ctrl+o Apply fix`, `Y Copy cmd`, `X Exclude`
(`detailsShortcuts`, `header.go`). The descriptions are at most ten cells: at 80 columns the
shortcut column is `78 - 19 (info) - 40 (logo) = 19` cells wide, `<ctrl+o>` takes nine of them, and
seven rows leave room for six entries beside `ctrl+p Commands` (`TestTheDetailHeaderHoldsItsSixKeysAtEveryWidth`
in `internal/app`). There is no `O`: `enter` opens the viewer, which has it. Each key is greyed,
never removed (Rule 130), by one `shortcut.Availability` that the header and the handler both read,
and a refused key puts its reason in the footer at level Warn and opens nothing. None of the
availabilities reads the disk, so a header redraw does no I/O.

| Key | Availability | Reasons | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enter` | `canOpenFindingFile` (`findingFilePath`) | `reasonNoFile`, `reasonFileOutsideTarget`, `reasonFileNotOnDisk` | in the Cmd, `staysInside` follows the links, then `uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: viewer.NewFileSource(path)}`; the viewer reports a missing file. A link that leaves the target gives `FindingFileRefusedMsg` and a Warn with `reasonFileLinkOutsideTarget` |
| `ctrl+o` | `canFixMisconfig` | `reasonNotMisconfigTab`, `reasonFileNotOnDisk`, the `Declines` reason, `noFixReason` | `prepareMisconfigFix`: the Misconfigurations tab's preview, confirmation (default No), write and re-scan |
| `Y` | `canCopyFixCommand` (`runCommand`) | `reasonNoCommand` | `writeClipboard(command)` in the Cmd, then `FixCommandCopiedMsg` |
| `X` | `canExclude` | `reasonNotASecret`, `reasonNotGitleaks` | `handleIgnoreSecret`: the confirmation of the results state, byte for byte |

`subjectFinding()` is what these actions act on: the finding on screen in the details state
(`selectedFinding`), the selected row in the results state. The detail never goes back through
`findingsTable.Selected()`, because a re-scan puts the table back at the top
(`setResult` runs `updateFindingsTable`, which runs `GotoTop`). In the detail the active tab is
the one the finding was opened from, so the tab checks of `canFixMisconfig` and `canExclude` stay
true to it. `ctrl+o` is a declared exception on the surface `security/details` (`app-shell.md`).
`reasonNotMisconfigTab` reads `Only misconfigurations have a built-in fix`, a wording that holds in
the detail as well as on a tab.

**Links.** `findingFilePath` is lexical (no I/O, so the header can call it on every frame): a
parent segment or an absolute path elsewhere is refused there. A link inside the target that points
outside it is only found by looking at the disk, so the Cmd of `enter` does it: `staysInside` applies
`filepath.EvalSymlinks` to the path and to the target and tests the relation again. A part of the
nothing is **offered** the fix: the pod-level setting changes nothing for those
that have one. Merge keys are refused everywhere in this scope, because a
`seccompProfile` they bring would be invisible; some valid manifests are refused
for that.

*Declines and the grey key.* `Rule.Declines func(scan.Finding) string` is a
refusal the finding alone settles, so `canFixMisconfig` greys the key with it,
without reading the file (Rule 130). It is set only for the seccomp rules, and
`seccompDeclines` answers only for KSV-0104 with `SeccompOrigin == "unconfined"`,
with the text of `MissingFor(f)` (DEVDESK-689). Every other refusal needs the
file, so it shows at the press of the key, in the footer at the Warn level, with
no modal; the key is lit until then. This is the same split as the host
namespaces. Widening `annotateSeccomp` to compute fixability at scan time was
rejected: a new `Finding` field in the cache and in the MCP `scan_result`, and a
value stale as soon as the file changes.

*Warning.* `Rule.Warning` (`seccompWarning`) is shown above the diff: `A workload
that ran without a seccomp filter may fail at run time under RuntimeDefault (a
blocked system call); the re-scan cannot detect that`. Trivy and the re-scan see
the manifest, not the behavior of the process; the safeguards are this text, the
modal that opens on No, and the user's version control.

# Cost of the change preview of the `:sec` finding detail (DEVDESK-753, H6)

Measurement note of 2026-11-23. It backs the decision on H6 of the plan ("is a loading state needed?").
A dated measure is never corrected afterwards: if the computation changes, add a new note.

| | |
|---|---|
| What is measured | `computeMisconfigFix(target, finding, scannedAt)` (`internal/ui/security/misconfig_change.go`): the whole of what the Cmd of the detail runs: `FixFor`, the lexical and link checks of the path, two `os.Stat`, the file read, the catalog's edits, `patch.Rewrite`, `patch.Diff`, the formatting of the lines, `scope`, and `git.StateOf` (a `git` process) |
| Fixture | the largest change of the catalog: `AVD-DS-0002` on a 3-line Dockerfile (a user, a group and a switch added: 11 lines of diff). `largestChangeFixture` in `details_change_perf_test.go` picks it by counting lines |
| Without git | `BenchmarkComputeMisconfigFix`, in a directory that is not a git repository: `go test -run xxx -bench BenchmarkComputeMisconfigFix -benchmem ./internal/ui/security` |
| With git | a throwaway test, not kept: `git init`, `git add`, `git commit` in a temporary directory, then 101 calls of `computeMisconfigFix`, sorted; median is the 51st, p95 the 96th |
| Machine | Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, 22 threads, Linux 6.12 (Debian 13), Go 1.27.4, git 2.47.3, warm page cache, local disk, nothing else measured at the same time |

## Results

| Case | Median | p95 | Max | Allocations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| not a git repository (the benchmark) | 1.04 ms | | | 124 KB, 456 allocs per call |
| not a git repository (101 calls) | 1.02 ms | 1.34 ms | 1.71 ms | |
| tracked and clean file in a git repository (101 calls) | 3.80 ms | 4.28 ms | 5.89 ms | |

`TestThePreviewOfTheLargestChangeIsFarUnderTheBudget` checks the median of 15 runs of the Cmd itself against
100 ms, so a computation that became slower by two orders of magnitude fails the suite without being flaky on a
loaded runner.

## Decision

The threshold of H6 was 100 ms at p95: the measure is 25 to 100 times under it. The computation is nonetheless
run by a Cmd, never in `Update` or `View` (Rule 110), because it reads the disk and starts `git`, and a file on
a network share or a repository on a slow disk can take much longer than this machine does. For that case, and
for the cell between the key press and the answer, the detail already shows `Change: preparing the preview...`
and the footer says `Preparing the change preview...` with the activity dot (`WantsBlink`). That costs one line
of status and removes any doubt about a slow disk, so it was kept even though, on this machine, the answer
arrives before the next frame.

## Limits

One machine, one fixture, a warm cache. `git.StateOf` is the part that scales with the repository (index size,
a slow filesystem); it was not measured on a large repository. The 100 ms budget of the test is a smoke alarm,
not a performance claim.

new='''### The Change section (DEVDESK-753)

The finding detail shows, under the Fix block and before `Why`, what the built-in fix would write, before
`ctrl+o` is pressed. The same computation feeds the section and the confirmation of `ctrl+o`, so what is shown
is what is written.

**One computation.** `computeMisconfigFix(target, finding, scannedAt)` (`misconfig_change.go`) is what
`prepareMisconfigFixCmd` used to do inline, and both Cmds call it: the preview of the detail
(`startChangePreview`, `details_change.go`) and the press of `ctrl+o`. Its pure part, `misconfigChangeOf`, takes
the rule, the relative path and the original bytes and returns `misconfigChange{File, Lines, Updated, Scope}`
without any I/O: `rule.Fix`, `patch.Rewrite`, `patch.Diff`, `changeLines`, `rule.ScopeOf`. The I/O part checks the
path lexically then through links, measures the files against the scan, reads the edited file and asks git
(`git.StateOf`, through `internal/git`, never `os/exec`). `MisconfigFixPreparedMsg.Lines` carries the formatted
diff next to the existing fields. `changeLines` drops the two header lines of `patch.Diff` (the file is named
by the label), indents `@@ line N @@` by two spaces so every line starts with `+`, `-` or a space, and runs each
line through `withoutControlSpace`: no ESC, OSC, bell, bidi mark or carriage return reaches the screen, while
`Updated` keeps the raw bytes that are written.

**State, kept by `Update` (Rule 110).** `Model.changePreview` holds `{Seq, Target, Finding, State, Prepared,
Failure}`; `previewSeq` numbers the requests and is never reset. `enter` on a finding calls `startChangePreview`,
which returns a Cmd only for a catalog rule on a directory that `misconfigFixAvailability` does not refuse
(never for a CVE, a secret, an image, a rule outside the catalog, or a refusal the finding alone settles) and
stores the state `previewPending`. The answer is a `ChangePreviewMsg{Seq, Target, Prepared}`; `handleChangePreview`
drops it unless the number, the target and `sameFinding` with the finding on screen all match, and unless the
detail is still open. `esc` resets the stored preview to its zero value, so a late answer finds no request. A
`WindowSizeMsg` starts nothing. The states:

| State | When | Section | `ctrl+o` |
|---|---|---|---|
| pending | asked, no answer yet | `Change: preparing the preview...`; footer `Preparing the change preview...` with the activity dot (`previewingStatus`, `WantsBlink` follows `status()`) | lit |
| ready | the change was computed | `Change: <file>`, the diff, `Git: <advice>` | lit |
| declined | the rule declines this instance, or the path is refused (outside the target, through a link) | `Change: none: DevDesk cannot write this fix` | greyed with the reason |
| expired | the file changed after the scan | `Change: stale preview: <file> changed after the scan`, no diff, no Git line | greyed with `reasonPreviewStale` |
| failed | unreadable, gone, rewrite error | `Change: preview failed: <file> cannot be read` (or `no longer exists`, or `the fix could not be computed — check logs`) | lit |

A failure puts `Could not preview the fix — check logs` in the footer at level Error, logs the cause, and never
shows `err.Error()` (`previewFailure` words the error). The detail stays usable: `W`, `enter` and scrolling work.
A failed preview leaves `ctrl+o` lit on purpose (H7): not knowing is not a no (Rule 130); the press computes the
fix again and reports its own error.

**One verdict, no disk read.** `previewVerdict(f)` is read by `canFixMisconfig` (the header and the handler of
`ctrl+o`) and by `fixStatus(f)` (the Fix line): for the stored preview of that same finding, expired and
declined give `Unavailable(reason)`, anything else is enabled. A finding other than the stored one, and any
state other than the detail, read the catalog alone. `fixStatus` turns a lit `Built-in fix available` into
`Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>` with the same reason the footer gives, so the Fix line, the grey key and the
footer after the press are one answer (`TestFixStatusAndTheShortcutAgreeOnAStoredPreview`).
`TestTheShortcutsAndTheFixLineReadNoDisk` removes the target directory and checks that `GetShortcuts`,
`canFixMisconfig`, `fixStatus` and the content do not change.

After a fix is written and the re-scan returns, `setResult` forgets the stored preview (the file was rewritten) and
`handleMisconfigVerified` asks again through `restartChangePreview`, which also rebuilds the viewport content so the
section reads `preparing the preview...` rather than a diff of the previous content. `setResult` resets to the zero
value rather than to "pending": a pending state with no Cmd behind it would wait for ever.

**The section.** `detailsChange` is written in `ColorText` alone, the labels in `DetailLabelStyle`, like the Fix block:
the markers `+` and `-` carry the meaning, never a red and a green. A ready preview is `Change: <file>` (the file the
fix edits, which is the `.dockerignore` for the build-context rule), the first 8 rows of the diff each cut by `oneLine`
to the column, `… N more lines` when there are more (`moreLines`, in `ColorText`), then `Git: <gitAdvice>`, the modal's
own text. A cut row can hide the only difference (DS-0011 adds a `/` at the end of a long `COPY`); the confirmation
has the row whole. For a vulnerability with a fixed version the line is `Change: <pkg> <version> -> <fixed>`
(`versionDelta`: the version `scan.PickFixed` chooses, the whole `FixedIn` when it cannot choose, as the command
DevDesk offers does), and never a diff: DevDesk does not write lockfiles. Everything else (a CVE with no fixed version,
a secret, a licence, an image, Helm, kubeconform or render failures, a rule outside the catalog) reads
`Change: none: DevDesk cannot write this fix`. The first line is in a closed vocabulary
(`TestEveryChangeLineIsInTheClosedVocabulary`, `closedChange`).

**Staleness.** The files the fix reads are measured against the end of the scan: a file whose modification time is
after `Result.EndTime` is refused with `reasonPreviewStale` (`The file changed after the scan — re-scan to preview the fix`),
`previewStale` being the comparison. Both the edited file and the finding's own file are checked (they differ for
the build-context rule). A zero `EndTime`, or no modification time, never makes a file stale. **Decision: `EndTime`, not
`StartTime`.** The plan (H2) proposed `StartTime` (`EndTime` when it is zero), stricter because a write during the
scan would count too; the criterion's own wording is the end of the scan, and that is what was built. A file written
while the scan was running and before it ended is therefore not flagged: a known gap. `patch.WriteIfUnchanged`
still guarantees that what is written is exactly what the confirmation showed. Limits of a time comparison: a tool
that restores modification times (`tar`, `rsync -t`), file systems with a one or two second granularity, clock skew on
a network file system.

**Hypotheses of the plan, as built.**

| | Hypothesis | Built as |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | 20 rules, not 22 | `remediation.catalog` has 20 keys (11 Dockerfile, 7 KSV, `BuildContextGitID`, `K8sAPIRemovedID`). `remediation.CatalogIDs()` lists them and the tests walk it, so the count of the criterion does not matter and a rule added without a fixture fails `TestEveryCatalogRuleHasAChangeFixture` |
| H2 | staleness threshold | see Staleness above: `EndTime`, not the plan's `StartTime` |
| H3 | the refusal is in the shared computation | so `ctrl+o` from the Misconfigurations tab is refused too, with the same Warn (see below) |
| H4 | a stale preview shows no diff | a diff computed on content the scan never read, with the scan's line numbers, may be wrong; the section says why, the modal is unreachable (the key is greyed) |
| H5 | the confirmation shows the same lines | the modal text is the rule's title, the warning, then `Lines` joined, then the file and its git advice; no `---`/`+++` header, `@@ line N @@` indented, ESC and OSC removed. The base-image modal of the Remediation tab is not touched |
| H6 | no loading state of its own | measured at about 1 ms without git and 4 ms with it (`docs/measurements/2026-11-23-sec-detail-change-preview.md`); the footer announcement was built anyway, since the computation reads the disk and starts `git` |
| H7 | a failed preview leaves `ctrl+o` lit | see the table above |

**What changes for `ctrl+o` on the Misconfigurations tab.** It goes through `computeMisconfigFix` too, so it gains
two refusals it did not have: a file whose modification time is after the end of the scan (`reasonPreviewStale`, a
Warn, nothing computed or written), and a path that reaches outside the target through a link
(`reasonFileLinkOutsideTarget`; the lexical `..` case already gave `reasonFileOutsideTarget`). Before, `ctrl+o` could
write through a symlink that leaves the scanned directory, and on a file changed since the scan. The confirmation
text also changes format: the same formatted lines as the section, with control characters removed, where the raw
`patch.Diff` text (with its `---`/`+++` header) used to be shown and could carry an escape sequence from the file.

'''
sub('### The Pod Security profile of a finding (DEVDESK-686)', new+'### The Pod Security profile of a finding (DEVDESK-686)')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Lot 2 (steps 3 to 6) is green. `mise run ci` exits 0 (fmt-check, vet host and windows, lint host and windows with 0 issues, build, `go test -race ./...`). `gofmt -l` is empty. The four requested `go test -count=1` packages pass. Nothing is committed.

**Changes**
- `internal/ui/security/details_change.go` (skeletons replaced): `startChangePreview`, `restartChangePreview`, `handleChangePreview`, `previewVerdict`, `fixStatus`, `previewingStatus`, `detailsChange`, `detailsPreview`, `versionDelta` and the helpers they use.
- `model.go`: `setResult` resets the stored preview. The SKELETON comment is removed.
- `findings.go`: `enter` calls `startChangePreview` and returns its Cmd. `update.go`: routes `ChangePreviewMsg`.
- `details.go`: `esc` clears the preview, `detailsFix` calls `m.fixStatus(f)`, and `detailsChange` is inserted after `detailsFix`.
- `view.go`: the footer says "Preparing the change preview..." with the activity dot while the preview is pending. `WantsBlink` follows it through `status()`.
- `misconfig_write.go`:
  - `canFixMisconfig` returns `previewVerdict` once the catalog part is enabled.
  - `prepareMisconfigFix` uses `m.scannedAt()`.
  - `handleMisconfigVerified` is split so the footer part is `verdictFooter`. It then batches `restartChangePreview()` with the footer Cmd.
- `header.go`: the "Finding details" help gets a Change paragraph after Effect and before "Why holds", and the intro sentence is updated. The word "Change" does not appear before "Effect", because the order test is strict.
- Docs:
  - `docs/architecture/scanning.md`: order diagram, new "The Change section (DEVDESK-753)" just before the Pod Security profile subsection, the `Declines` paragraph, and the `ctrl+o` table row.
  - New `docs/measurements/2026-11-23-sec-detail-change-preview.md`.

**Review of the tester's edits to existing tests**
- None of them weakens a test.
- `details_test.go`: `blockLabels` gains `Change:`.
- `details_fix_test.go`: it now uses `m.fixStatus(f)` and also asserts it equals `fixStatusOf(f, onDisk)` when nothing is stored. That is stricter.
- `details_fix_flow_test.go`: `fixDetail` answers the preview Cmd as the runtime would. In `TestPreparingTheFixDoesNotAnnounceARescan`, the `|| m.status().Activity` clause is dropped. The "Re-scanning" check stays. This is a legitimate accommodation of the new "Preparing the change preview..." announcement.
- I changed no test.

**Measurement** (Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, git 2.47.3, largest fixture AVD-DS-0002 with 11 diff lines)
- Without git: median 1.02 ms, p95 1.34 ms. `BenchmarkComputeMisconfigFix` gives 1.04 ms per call.
- With git, tracked and clean file: median 3.8 ms, p95 4.3 ms.
- The 100 ms threshold from H6 is not reached. The footer announcement is built anyway, as you asked.

**Deviations and open points**
1. `setResult` resets the preview to its zero value, not to "pending". A "pending" state with no Cmd behind it would wait forever. `handleMisconfigVerified` then restarts the preview and rebuilds the viewport content, so the section reads "preparing the preview..." after the verdict. The behaviour you described is observable and tested.
2. For the "stale preview: <file> changed after the scan" line and the failure line, the file named is `Finding.File`. For the build-context rule the stale file may be the `.dockerignore`. Naming it exactly would need `errDeclined` to carry the file, which touches lot 1 code, so I did not do it.
3. The staleness decision is documented as `EndTime`, as you asked. The plan's H2 stricter variant, `StartTime`, is not retained, so a write during the scan is not flagged. This is stated in `scanning.md`.
4. The `git`-case measurement used a throwaway test that I deleted. It is not reproducible from the repo, and the measurement note says so. It was measured on one machine only.
5. The 752 session's `details.go` and `header.go` edits may conflict with mine in these places: the `buildDetailsContent` list, the `detailsFix` first line, and the "Finding details" help text. The edits are small and mechanical.
